doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Working as a contractor and organist
title: Electronic keyboards, split keyboards and the mini Moog
summary: Rowe watched his left hand at the Beeches. They discuss the electronic keyboard and the mini Moog Montalbano bought from Rowe.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well I got my education, watching — because I used to sit at the Beeches, I mean that was a big thing for me. I don’t know if you realize. That gig was a big thing for me. For one thing, watching you guys operate. But also because I used to sit at the left end of the organ and I’d watch your hand. I’d go, oh, I have to learn how to do that. It must have been a pretty big thing when they came out with an electronic keyboard that had a decent piano sound and that you could split the keyboard.

Yes. It made things a lot easier to work. And of course, like you, I bought that mini Moog from you. I used to carry that thing around and put it on top of the Rhodes. It was always one keyboard or another. A little synthesizer you’d put on top, or sometimes it would be over to the left so I learned how to play like this, and totally wrecked my back of course. Now everything’s just one. Yeah. It’s a lot nicer.
